uncited: Coarse-to-Fine Hierarchical Sampling is a strategy that improves the learning of high-frequency details in Neural Radiance Fields by performing two tiers of volume sampling .

It solves the problem of inefficient uniform sampling, where most samples fall in empty space, by using a coarse network to identify opaque regions and then clustering a second set of samples near those regions to train a fine network .

It sets itself apart from standard uniform sampling by adaptively concentrating computational effort on visible geometry, and from its sibling [TermiNeRF](8828-terminerf.md) by not explicitly modeling termination probabilities but rather relying on opacity-based importance sampling .
All methods in this family aim to maintain visual fidelity while reducing the total number of volume queries .
The concept was introduced in the original NeRF paper (Mildenhall et al., 2020) as a way to mitigate the inefficiency of uniform sampling .
It became a standard component in subsequent NeRF variants due to its ability to allocate samples to geometrically relevant regions.
